summary: The unit now uses KillMode=none, so a rejected or timed-out stop hook no longer falls through to control-group SIGTERM/SIGKILL; the new tests pin that setting, verify rejection paths exit 1 without sending Browser.close or signals, verify a successful stop still sends Browser.close, and an isolated systemd fixture proves fixture processes survive past the stop timeout. No actionable defects found.

evidence: systemd/user/ubiquity-sales-nav-browser.service lines 15-19 set KillMode=none, giving systemd no kill instruction to apply after a rejected or timed-out ExecStop.
tests/sales-nav-browser-stop.test.ts lines 23-32 pin KillMode=none together with the guarded ExecStop, Restart, and ExecStart settings.

tests/sales-nav-browser-stop.test.ts lines 130-155 prove wrong-profile, changed-PID, and unreachable-DevTools rejections exit 1 with no Browser.close and no signals, while a successful stop still sends Browser.close.
tests/sales-nav-browser-stop.test.ts lines 162-227 run an isolated systemd user unit with the unit KillMode and assert both fixture processes remain alive past TimeoutStopSec after ExecStop rejects.
